Regex lab (calculator, cheat sheet and pattern library)

Test a regular expression against sample values, preview the URL a rewrite rule produces with $0 $1 … captures, and browse FortiWeb/FortiADC-oriented examples before the pattern goes into a rule.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
📍 WhereTop bar → Tools (wrench) → Regex calculator / Regex cheat sheet / Pattern library; also the ".*" button beside regex fields

What is it?#

The regex lab is a pattern calculator for the regular expressions you type into FortiWeb and FortiADC rules — URL access rules, exceptions, URL rewriting, content routing and rewriting, custom signatures. You type a pattern and some real sample values, and it shows which samples match, what each capture group holds and, on the rewrite tab, the exact string each sample is rewritten to.

What does it do?#

  • Match tester — runs the pattern against every sample (one per line) and highlights the matched part; captures are shown as $0=…, $1=… in the appliance's zero-based numbering ($0 is the first ( … ) group).
  • Rewrite / $captures — adds a Replacement field and shows sample → output for every matching sample ($0 $1 … $9, ${n}, and \1 are accepted; $0 and \1 both name the first group). Non-matching samples are shown as no match — passes through unchanged.
  • Library — curated examples for the product and, when opened from a field, for that kind of field. Clicking an example loads the pattern, a sample and (for rewrite examples) the replacement.
  • Cheat sheet — anchors, character classes, quantifiers, groups and alternation, lookarounds and escapes, each with an example.
  • Flavor notes — practical notes for the selected product (FortiWeb or FortiADC), shown beside the tester.
  • Engine honesty — every verdict states it was Judged server-side by Python re — an approximation of the PCRE engine on FortiWeb / FortiADC. When the pattern uses a construct where the two engines differ, the footer turns into This verdict may not match the appliance. and names the construct.

Requirements#

None. The lab never contacts an appliance and never writes to the database.

Permissions#

Any signed-in user.

How to use#

Test a pattern#

  1. Open Tools → Regex calculator.
  2. Pick FortiWeb or FortiADC in the header (it defaults to the ADOM you are in).
  3. Type the pattern in Pattern, for example ^/admin(/.*)?$.
  4. Paste values into Test samples — one per line, ideally real URLs, hosts or parameter values.
  5. Tick Case-insensitive if the rule is case-insensitive.
  6. The verdict updates as you type: N of M sample(s) match.

Preview a rewrite#

  1. Open the Rewrite / $captures tab.
  2. Enter the pattern, for example ^/old-shop/(.*)$.
  3. Enter the Replacement, for example /new-shop/$0 — $0 is the first ( … ) group, as on the appliance.
  4. Read the output for each sample: /old-shop/item/42 → /new-shop/item/42.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the rewrite preview, examples, cheat sheet and group labels use the FortiWeb/FortiADC numbering ($0 = first group); a replacement written for the old preview ($1 for the first group) must be shifted down by one.

Use the lab from a rule field#

On the Exceptions page and in the object editor, regex-capable fields have a .* button (Regex calculator — test this pattern against samples). It opens the lab with the field's current value, the field type shown next to the title, and examples for that field. When the pattern is right, click Use this pattern to copy it back into the field.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Pattern Regular expression, up to 2,048 characters Yes ^/api/v[0-9]+/
Replacement Rewrite tab only; $0–$9 ($0 = first group), ${n}, \1, $$ for a literal $ No /item?id=$0
Case-insensitive Applies the ignore-case flag No ticked
Test samples Up to 100 lines, 4,096 characters each No /shop/checkout.php

Example#

🧪Example — Strip the .html suffix

Pattern ^/(.*)\.html$, replacement /$0, sample /about.html. The rewrite tab shows /about.html → /about and $0=about.

💡Tip

An unanchored pattern matches anywhere in the value. Use ^ and $ when you mean the whole string, and escape literal dots (\.php$).

Result#

Nothing is saved and nothing is audited. Use this pattern only fills the field on the page; you still save the rule normally.

Troubleshooting#

"invalid regex: …"#

Possible causes - The pattern is not valid in Python's re engine. This includes several constructs that are valid on the appliance: \K, \R, \h, \z, \p{…}, (?R), (?&name), PCRE-style named groups (?<name>…) and an inline flag such as (?i) placed in the middle of the pattern.

Solution 1. Read the footer: when it says This verdict may not match the appliance. the pattern may still be accepted by FortiWeb/FortiADC. 2. To test the logic here, rewrite the construct temporarily (for example (?P<name>…) instead of (?<name>…), (?i) at the very start).

A sample matches here but not on the appliance (or the reverse)#

Possible causes - \d, \w, \s and \b match Unicode characters in Python but only ASCII in PCRE (unless UCP is enabled). \Z behaves differently before a final newline.

Solution 1. Prefer explicit classes such as [0-9] and [A-Za-z0-9_].

"empty pattern"#

Possible causes - The Pattern field is empty.

"invalid replacement: it names more capture groups than the pattern has (N) -- $0 is the first ( … ) group"#

Possible causes - The replacement references a group the pattern does not have — often $1 used for the first group out of habit.

Solution 1. Count from zero: the first ( … ) group is $0, the second $1.

The "Use this pattern" button is missing#

Possible causes - The lab was opened from the Tools menu, not from a field's .* button. There is no field to copy into.

Advanced#

Advanced Capture numbering

The preview follows Fortinet's zero-based numbering: $0 (or ${0}) is the first parenthesised group, $1 the second, and so on; there is no reference to the whole match. A \1 backreference keeps its usual one-based meaning, so \1 and $0 name the same group. This numbering follows Fortinet's documentation; confirm a new rewrite on a test policy before relying on it. On FortiADC Content Rewriting, captures from the Host regex and the URL regex of the same rule are numbered together, so tested alone a URL regex's group is $0, but paired with a Host regex in one rule it becomes $1.

Advanced Limits

Python's re has no timeout, so the lab caps the pattern (2,048 characters), the replacement (2,048), the sample count (100) and the sample length (4,096). Endpoints: GET /regex-lab/examples, POST /regex-lab/test, POST /regex-lab/rewrite.
